extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media professionals, and readers concerned about AI and media ethics
extracted.subtask_short: investigative news on AI in media
extracted.subtask_description: An investigative news article examining use of AI-generated authors, AI-written articles, and related ethical, editorial, and disclosure failures at mainstream publishers. Focus is on evaluating publisher practices and the trustworthiness of published content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bylines and authorship transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines exist for a reason: they give credit where it's due, and just as importantly, they let readers hold writers accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish content under fake or nonexistent author names. If an author byline is changed or content is reattributed, include an editor's note explaining the reason for the change and who actually produced the piece so readers can hold creators accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI use and third-party creation
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the articles credited to Ortiz or the other names contained any disclosure about the use of AI; later disclaimers mentioned only that the content was 'created by a 3rd party.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly disclose when content is produced or substantially assisted by AI or by an external/licensed third party. Disclosures should specify the nature of AI involvement and whether in-house editorial staff participated in editing or oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of author identity and bios
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should not present fabricated biographies or personas (e.g., 'stay-at-home dad', 'information analyst') as real people when those profiles are untraceable or supported by AI-generated headshots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify authors' real identities and professional claims before publishing. Do not rely on vendor-supplied bios without independent checks; remove or flag bios that cannot be corroborated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image provenance and headshot verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile photos used were traceable to a website that sells AI-generated headshots, indicating images may be synthetic rather than real staff photos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the source and provenance of author headshots; avoid using AI-generated or stock images presented as real people. If images are synthetic or licensed, disclose that fact to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality, formatting, and editorial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated posts often show bizarre language, factual errors, and glaring formatting discrepancies (e.g., numbered lists that repeat '1'), indicating insufficient editorial control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure human editing and copyediting to catch awkward phrasing, formatting errors, and illogical claims. Maintain baseline readability and structural norms before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated content has produced factual mistakes and plagiarism at other publishers, prompting corrections; accuracy cannot be assumed for machine-generated text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same fact-checking rigor to AI-assisted or third-party content as to in-house reporting. Verify factual claims, sources, and originality prior to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of anti-plagiarism and anti-AI detection tools
rubrics_metrics.description: AdVon claimed to follow a policy that involves using both counter-plagiarism and counter-AI software on all content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement and routinely audit anti-plagiarism and AI-detection tools as part of editorial workflow, but do not treat vendor tool-claims as sole proof — validate effectiveness and results independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendor oversight and verification of partner claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arena Group's investigation appears to have relied on asking the vendor whether the content was AI-generated and taking their word for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct independent audits of partner-produced content rather than relying solely on vendor assurances. Monitor partner output continuously and terminate partnerships when practices violate editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetization transparency and conflict disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated buying guides were monetized by affiliate links that provide financial kickbacks, raising ethical concerns when combined with undisclosed third-party production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose affiliate relationships and any financial incentives connected to product coverage. Ensure monetization does not compromise editorial independence or mislead readers about objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction policy and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers like CNET issued corrections after AI-driven errors were revealed; timely corrections are necessary when mistakes are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a clear, visible corrections policy and apply it promptly to AI- or vendor-generated errors. Publicly acknowledge errors and explain remedial actions and policy changes to restore trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of editorial involvement and role clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: A later disclaimer noted that 'Sports Illustrated editorial staff are not involved in the creation of this content' but earlier pages lacked such clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers explicitly what role (if any) in-house editors and journalists had in creating, editing, or approving third-party content. Where editorial staff are uninvolved, state that clearly at publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of deceptive pseudonyms or concealment
rubrics_metrics.description: AdVon had writers use a pen or pseudo name in certain articles to protect author privacy — actions the publisher said it does not condone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use pseudonyms or fabricated bylines to hide the true origin of content in ways that mislead readers; if pseudonyms are used for legitimate safety/privacy reasons, disclose that context transparently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traceability and archival integrity of published content
rubrics_metrics.description: Fake personas and their articles were periodically scrubbed and reattributed to new names with no editor's note explaining the change in byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve an auditable record of who produced content and any subsequent changes; when deleting or reattributing pieces, provide an explanation to readers rather than silently removing or rewriting history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility for aggregated/licensed content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arena Group stated the questioned pieces were licensed content from an external company, implying a need for oversight even for licensed material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume editorial responsibility for any licensed or syndicated content you publish: vet quality, verify sources, and ensure licensing arrangements do not circumvent editorial standards or transparency requirements.
